title: 8 Automated classification of FAMACHA scores using Machine Learning Models for Anemia detection in small ruminants
content:
Abstract
Precise classification of FAMACHA scores is important for evaluating anemia in small ruminants and enhancing parasite management strategies in livestock agriculture. FAMACHA scores vary from 1 to 5, where 1 and 2 denote healthy animals, and 4 and 5 signify severe anemia. Data was collected using Samsung A54 smart phone weekly over 4 months of time for lower eye conjunctiva. Conventional techniques for assessing FAMACHA scores are subjective and labor-intensive, necessitating visual examination and professional analysis. This research employs machine learning algorithms to automate the classification of visual FAMACHA data. Three models, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), were assessed based on their precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy across the five FAMACHA categories. The SVM model attained the highest mean accuracy (84.6%), with precision varying from 71% to 100%, recall from 72% to 94%, and F1-score from 76% to 95% across the five categories. It notably excelled in identifying FAMACHA 4 and 5 classes, with absolute precision (100%) for each. The BPNN model exhibited consistent performance, attaining an average accuracy of 84%, with precision ranging from 80% to 100%, recall from 78% to 92%, and F1-score from 79% to 93%. The CNN model exhibited the lowest average accuracy at 75.8%, attributable to elevated misclassification rates. The precision varied between 64% and 95%, recall between 66% and 87%, and F1-score between 71% and 91%. The CNN model encountered difficulties, specifically with the FAMACHA 1 and 4 classes, misclassifying samples owing to nuanced variations in picture characteristics. The findings indicate that SVM is the most dependable model for identifying FAMACHA scores, especially in resource-constrained environments. The BPNN demonstrated commendable performance, providing a good tradeoff between precision and recall. The CNN model necessitates additional optimization, such as augmenting the dataset size or modifying its architecture, to enhance its generalization capability. Future studies may investigate ensemble learning methodologies to amalgamate the advantages of these models, hence improving accuracy and practical utility in animal health monitoring systems.
